fields.meta_title: Contact Form Builder That Routes Every Message | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a contact form that routes every message by topic, stores it in a database you own and reminds its owner if nobody replies. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Contact Form That Reaches the Right Person
fields.hero_description: Name your visitors' topics and who answers each. Emergent builds the contact form, routes every message to its owner and keeps the history in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Contact Form Should Do After Send
fields.features_subheading: Each one keeps a message from sitting unread in an inbox nobody owns.
fields.feature_1:
Routing by topic

Pick an owner for every kind of question a visitor might ask. The topic they choose decides who gets the message, and whether that person hears about it by email or in Slack.
fields.feature_2:
Fields that fit the topic

Show an order number field only to someone asking about an order, and a guest count only for catering. A visitor with a general question sees the short form and nothing more.
fields.feature_3:
Every message saved as a row

Keep each message in a database you own, with its topic and reply status on the same row as the sender. Search past conversations by email address, or export the table at any time.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders when nobody replies

Give each topic a reply window. A message still unanswered when the window closes sends a reminder to its owner, then escalates to a manager you named when you built the form.
fields.feature_5:
A confirmation the sender can keep

Email every sender a copy of their message with a reference number. When they quote it in a follow-up, support finds the original row in one search instead of asking again.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take anywhere

Export the contact form and its database to GitHub on paid plans, routing rules included. A developer can host it on your own servers or drop it into the website you already run.
fields.why_title: Why Build Your Contact Form With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A template hands you the fields. Emergent builds the form with the rules that decide who answers, and you change either one by prompting.

fields.tab_content_1:
Catering questions land with one person

Larkspur Bakery's contact page asks every visitor to pick a topic first. Catering opens two more fields: the kind of event and the number of guests. Those messages go to Dana Whitfield, the events manager, by email. Everything else lands in the shared inbox the counter staff check each morning.
fields.tab_content_2:
Support opens each ticket with the order attached

Customers of Fernhill Goods write in from a phone and enter their order number with the message. The form looks it up in the store's Shopify orders and opens a ticket that shows the items and when they shipped. A customer reporting a damaged mug can add a photo before sending.
fields.tab_content_3:
Any message unanswered for 4 hours moves up a level

Three clinics share one form at Cedar Row Physical Therapy. Patients pick a location, and the message goes to that clinic's front desk. If nobody replies within 4 business hours, Lena Park, the practice manager, gets it in Slack. She sees which desk let it sit and for how long.
fields.tab_content_4:
A reporter on a 48-hour deadline gets a direct line

Reporters writing about Northwind use the get in touch form on its press page. It asks for the outlet, the story and the deadline. A deadline within 48 hours sends a direct Slack message to Jonah Reyes, the communications lead. Later deadlines join a press queue he reviews each Monday.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Contact Form
fields.howto_description: Decide who answers before you decide what to ask. The fields follow from the people on the other end.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set a reply window per topic
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the topics people write in about, such as orders, catering or press, and put one named person beside each. Add a fallback owner for anything that fits none of them. That list becomes the routing behind the form.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask everyone for a name, an email address and the message. Add a phone field only when a person will call back. Every required field you add is one more thing a visitor has to fill in before they can send.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Make the topic the first question, with one choice per owner on your list plus Something else. Each choice can open its own fields: an order number for orders, a guest count for catering, a deadline for press.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide how long each kind of message may wait before its owner is reminded. A broken order might get one business day, while a partnership pitch can wait a week. Name the manager who hears about anything past its window.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write your topics and their owners into one prompt in plain English, with the fields and reply windows. Emergent builds the form, the rules that route each message and a table where every message is stored. Change any owner later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Draft the email each sender receives: a thank-you line, a copy of what they wrote and a reference number. If you state a reply time, pick one you can meet on your busiest week, not your quietest.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Embed it and send a test
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place the form on your contact page, or share the hosted link on a custom domain (built into Emergent, uses credits). Send one test message per topic from a phone. Check that each one reaches its owner and that the confirmation lands in the sender's inbox.

plan.angle: Half of the top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Cognito, Typeform, Formplus, Formester); the rest is guides on which fields to ask for (Taboola, Mailpro, freecontactform). Every one stops at the Send button. This page covers the fields briefly, then shows what a contact form does after Send: each message goes to the person who handles that topic, carries the order or location it is about, and gets escalated when nobody replies.

chip_prompts: Build a contact form for my website where visitors pick a topic first, and send orders, catering, and press questions to the person who answers each one.
On my contact form, ask catering visitors for the event date and head count, and ask anyone with an order problem for the order number and a photo.
If a message on my contact form goes unanswered for one business day, remind the person who owns that topic, and escalate it to me the next morning.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Contact Form That Reaches the Right Person" and hero ("builds the contact form, routes every message to its owner and keeps the history in a database you own") cover the form's whole job.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is builder templates and what-is guides; the page defines the form (FAQ 1), shows four business-type examples, a 7-step how-to, free options (FAQ 3) and Contact Form 7 answers from PAA.

specificity.evidence: "Show an order number field only to someone asking about an order, and a guest count only for catering"; table rows are form-builder dimensions (response caps, where responses live).

openers.evidence: "Larkspur Bakery's contact page asks every visitor to pick a topic first." "Three clinics share one form at Cedar Row Physical Therapy." Feature bodies open on verbs: "Pick", "Show", "Keep", "Give", "Email", "Export".

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q6/Q7 clean; serial-comma drift in one chip prompt and an awkward parenthetical recorded as notes.

voice.evidence: Concrete and unglamorous: "a damaged mug", "the shared inbox the counter staff check each morning", "a press queue he reviews each Monday".

truth.evidence: Contact Form 7 facts match wordpress.org and the Flamingo page in domain_sources; Emergent claims map to claims_used (custom-domain, free-start, code-export, alerts); table from the library.

distinct.evidence: Built around routing messages to owners with reply windows, not lead capture or quotes; no sibling primary (lead capture form, quote form, demo request form) in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions (7 from PAA), each answered first; hub link in item 2 ("AI form builder"); exact-match links "registration form" and "intake form".

images.evidence: Catering, 80 guests, sent to Dana Whitfield by email; order #10482 with mug photo opens a Shopify-backed ticket; Midtown 4h 20m escalated to Lena Park in Slack while Harbor 3h 15m stays open; 36 hours < 48 triggers the DM to Jonah Reyes.
